guard: public history abort stops the active JetStream pull and dashboard deadlines pass that abort to every unfinished source
why: M1 removes the abort listener from the active drainWindow iterator. It restores the live defect:
the public channelHistory promise stays pending and its consumer remains on the broker after the
caller aborts. The suite drives the real public API over a real constrained connection.
M2 removes the dashboard's signal from channel history calls. It uses the existing bounded
aggregation suite's deterministic source seam, which asserts every started source receives the
shared signal and observes it aborted at the response deadline. This is a constructed seam for
the web threading only; M1 is the real entry-point proof for broker work cancellation.
Both anchors are unique code-only lines. Each mutation names the first assertion that must turn red.
